title: The Tax Crackdown Isn’t Over
gist: Gavekal teaser: China's crackdown on mainland residents' offshore trusts produced over RMB160bn of declared income tax (at least RMB120bn paid in October 2026, a record month), and the selling to fund those bills likely deepened Hong Kong's stock decline; the title signals more enforcement ahead.

insights.claim: China required mainland residents to declare and pay, by October 22, 2026, sometimes years of back taxes on offshore trusts that company founders had used partly to shield holdings in offshore-listed firms.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Founders of offshore-listed Chinese firms face a new tax liability on trust-held stakes, a structural shift for that ownership model.
insights.quote: Mainland residents had until October 22 to declare and pay sometimes years of back taxes on their offshore trusts

insights.claim: China's State Taxation Administration said the offshore-trust tax crackdown produced declarations of more than RMB160bn in income taxes, with at least RMB120bn paid in October 2026.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Implies roughly RMB40bn or more of declared tax still to be paid, a possible ongoing source of forced selling.
insights.quote: the crackdown had led to the declaration of more than RMB160bn in income taxes, of which at least RMB120bn was paid in October
insights.locator: Last week, the State Taxation Administration

insights.claim: The offshore-trust back-tax payments made October 2026 the biggest month of income-tax collection in China's history.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Signals Beijing's willingness to aggressively tax wealthy offshore holdings as a fiscal source; watch for further enforcement, as the title says the crackdown isn't over.
insights.quote: That’s a big enough sum to make October 2026 the biggest month of income-tax collection in China’s history

insights.claim: China's offshore-trust tax bills probably worsened Hong Kong's stock-market decline because some taxpayers sold shares to pay them.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tax-driven selling is a non-fundamental flow on Hong Kong equities; if enforcement continues, expect further supply pressure on founder-held offshore-listed stocks.
insights.quote: probably exacerbated Hong Kong’s stock-market decline as some taxpayers sold shares to pay their bills
